answer: Prove every identity sits behind a distinct network vantage point. Five independent probes ping the agent and triangulate its latency, building an atlas of real locations where no two identities may share one spot. A second identity from the same connection is refused at once, and a caught proxy farm loses every identity it holds. Faking 1,000 locations needs 1,000 residential lines at 40 dollars a month each, about 480,000 dollars a year, plus hardware no rented nebula of proxies can hide. Like a plume of smoke, each real agent rises from exactly one chimney.
